meta.description: Build UpSet plots to visualize set intersections beyond 4 sets (where Venn fails) using ComplexUpset (modern, ggplot2-grammar) or the unmaintained UpSetR, with explicit cardinality vs degree sorting, attribute panels, and query highlighting. Use when comparing overlap across many gene sets, peak sets, variant lists, or any set membership matrix where Venn diagrams become illegible.
meta.execution_note: Executed 5/5 inputs on the data-visualization env: R 4.4.3 (ComplexUpset 1.3.3, UpSetR 1.4.0, ggplot2 4.0.3, patchwork 1.3.2, msigdbr 26.1.0) and Python 3.12 (upsetplot 0.9.0 in venv-pd2 with pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.5.3, matplotlib 3.11.2; the main pandas 3.0.6 venv was run to record its failure). Every code block in SKILL.md and both shipped examples were run. Every figure was checked against an independent set-operation truth (two implementations, R and Python, agreed) by reading what was drawn (ggplot_build layer data, grob trees, matplotlib artists) and 11 PNGs were opened. Data: SYNTHETIC planted 8-set data (D is a strict subset of A, H is empty, seed-free by construction), the Skill's own 4-set toy, the shipped example's simulated 6 sets, and REAL MSigDB Hallmark sets (10 immune/inflammatory sets). One extra private ComplexUpset build against ggplot2 3.5.2 was made inside the audit folder to test the Skill's pin advice; no shared env was changed.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI, statistic or result; the three cited papers (Lex 2014, Conway 2017, Krassowski) are real. Several factual statements do not hold (ComplexUpset 'CRAN active through 2025-07' when 1.3.3 of 2021-12-11 is current, fromList duplicates 'inflate counts', 2^N columns, mode='intersect' as a 1-set fix); recorded as accuracy defects, not invented evidence.

practice_boundaries.detail: Visualization Skill; no diagnostic or prescriptive content.

methodological_ground.detail: Every intersection count the packages draw equals the independent set computation in all 5 inputs (exclusive counts, ordering, set sizes, degree filtering, min_size, subset-of-another set). The Skill's advice creates silently wrong figures in two places (UpSetR nsets=4 on more than 4 sets; NA/blank IDs counted as shared genes) but never inverts a conclusion; both are P1.

code_usability.detail: Borderline. The R route (ComplexUpset block 1, sorting, annotations with columns present, UpSetR block, shipped upset_gene_sets.R) runs and draws correctly. The Python route does not run as shipped on the installed stack: every snippet uses show_counts=True, which raises TypeError at savefig with numpy 2.5.3 even in the pandas-2 venv, the main pandas-3 venv fails earlier with 'Invalid RGBA argument: nan', and the shipped upset_python.py also has a stack-independent bug (data.to_frame() on a DataFrame). With show_counts=False the Python route is correct. Recorded as P1 rather than a veto because the R route is the Skill's stated primary tool and a workaround exists; a Python-only user would be blocked.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 3, correctness 2, appropriateness 3. Covers ComplexUpset, UpSetR and upsetplot with sorting, queries and annotations, and the plotted numbers are right. Several stated behaviours do not reproduce: 'duplicates inflate fromList counts', degree sort 'descending' shows 3-set groups first, mode='intersect' does not remove 1-set bars, style_subsets(present=) highlights supersets, intersection_plot_elements is a height not a cap, 1023 columns for 10 sets (137 real).

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 2, error reporting 2, recoverability 3. Empty sets are dropped without a message by ComplexUpset and UpSetR, UpSetR nsets=4 silently keeps only the 4 largest sets, NA and '' IDs count as shared genes, a second upset_query on an empty intersection crashes render with a cryptic aesthetics error, upsetplot fails at savefig.

performance_context.note: Token cost 2, efficiency 3. 248-line SKILL.md plus an 88-line usage-guide.md that restates the same tips, failure modes and prompts; no references/ layer.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 3, consistency 2, feedback 3, error prevention 3. Goal/Approach blocks and a failure-mode section help. Inconsistent: text says cardinality sort is the default (true for ComplexUpset, false for upsetplot, whose default is degree), the blocks pair 'descending' with a degree sort the text describes as 1-set first, and a 4-set toy where every bar is 1 cannot show any sorting.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 4, forgiveness 2. Natural example prompts; off-spec inputs (empty set, NA, more sets than nsets) fail silently instead of asking.

security.note: No credentials, network, eval or shell. Examples write PDFs/PNGs to the cwd and overwrite silently.

maintainability.note: Modularity 2, modifiability 3, testability 2. Everything in one SKILL.md plus two examples; the Python example cannot run (to_frame) and its third plot has no working path; no known-answer test data.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision 4, progressive disclosure 3, composability 3, idempotency 4, escape hatches 2. Related Skills exist as folders. No guidance on when not to draw an UpSet plot beyond 'too many sets'; both R packages export upset() and the Skill never warns that attaching both masks one.

key_strengths: Every intersection count, order, set size and filter that was drawn matched an independent set computation: 14/14 planted bars (including a set that is a strict subset of another), 137 real Hallmark intersections across ComplexUpset, UpSetR and upsetplot, and boxplot/stacked-fraction panels equal the per-intersection statistics.
The shipped R example and the UpSetR block run and draw correctly, with query highlights on exactly the named intersections.

The 'single-set exclusives dominate' failure mode is real on real gene sets (8 of the top 8 bars), and the ComplexUpset vs UpSetR choice and the min_degree / intersections filters are the right tools for it.

Filters that the Skill teaches (n_intersections, intersections=list(), min_degree, min_size) and the upsetplot filters (min_subset_size, max_subset_rank, min/max_degree) all behaved exactly as filtered truth.

recommendations.title: Python upsetplot route does not run as shipped
recommendations.problem: Every Python snippet uses show_counts=True: with numpy 2.5.3 it raises TypeError at savefig (upsetplot 0.9.0 passes a 1-element array to Axes.text), and a plain pip install brings pandas 3, where UpSet fails with 'Invalid RGBA argument: nan'. examples/upset_python.py also calls data.to_frame() on the DataFrame that from_contents returns, so its metadata plot cannot run on any version. A Python-only user gets no figure.
recommendations.root_cause: Version stamp says only 'upsetplot 0.9+'; the snippets were not run against a current stack.
recommendations.fix: State the working stack (pandas < 3 for upsetplot 0.9.0) and drop show_counts=True or show a labelling workaround; fix the example: build the attribute frame from from_contents' DataFrame (df['log2FC'] = ...), do not call to_frame(); run the example in CI.

recommendations.title: Query highlighting breaks; the Skill blames the wrong cause
recommendations.problem: Block 3 as written raises a render error on the Skill's own data (the second query targets an empty exclusive intersection), and two queries on non-adjacent existing bars draw a highlight rectangle 6.3 bar-widths wide over neighbouring bars, on ggplot2 4.0.3 and 3.5.2. The Skill attributes ComplexUpset trouble to ggplot2 4.0 (issue #213) and advises pinning ggplot2, which does not fix this. Block 4 as written fails because log2FC/significant are not in df.
recommendations.root_cause: Queries were not rendered with two targets; the 4-set example has no intersection larger than 1 and no empty query target.
recommendations.fix: Use targets that exist, test with two non-adjacent bars, document the width behaviour (or a working alternative such as separate single-query plots or a colour column in base_annotations), remove or correct the ggplot2 4.0 claim, and add the missing columns to block 4's df.

recommendations.title: Silent data-loss patterns are not warned about
recommendations.problem: UpSetR nsets = 4 on a longer list keeps the 4 largest sets and draws merged, wrong bars (A-only 17 vs 12); empty sets vanish from both R plots without a message; NA and '' IDs are counted as shared elements (3 shared instead of 1).
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's blocks hardcode nsets and never validate set sizes, emptiness or identifiers before plotting.
recommendations.fix: Add a pre-plot checklist: nsets = length(sets); stop on empty sets; drop NA/'' and normalise IDs; print set sizes and the union size and compare with the sum of drawn bars.

recommendations.title: Several stated behaviours are false or unreproduced
recommendations.problem: (a) 'duplicates in fromList inflate counts' and the reconciliation row on duplicate handling: not reproduced in UpSetR or ComplexUpset (upsetplot raises instead). (b) 'ComplexUpset CRAN active through 2025-07': 1.3.3 of 2021-12-11 is the current release. (c) 'ggplot2 4.0 broke upset()': upset() builds on 4.0.3. (d) mode='intersect' as a way to exclude 1-set bars: it makes them the full set size. (e) degree sort shown with 'descending' puts 3-set groups first. (f) style_subsets(present=) is called a specific intersection but highlights supersets. (g) intersection_plot_elements is called a cap on intersections but is a height. (h) 2^10 = 1023 columns: 137 drawn on real data.
recommendations.root_cause: Claims were written from documentation and memory, not checked against an installed stack.
recommendations.fix: Correct or delete each statement using the measured behaviour (exclude 1-set with min_degree=2 or an intersections list; sort_intersections='ascending' for degree; add absent= to style_subsets; use max_subset_rank for a cap).

recommendations.title: The canonical toy example cannot show anything
recommendations.problem: In the Skill's 4-set example every gene has a unique membership, so all eight bars are 1: sorting, counts, queries and attribute panels cannot be told apart from noise. The example's n_intersections=20 and its second query target an empty intersection.
recommendations.root_cause: Hand-made toy sets without planted overlaps.
recommendations.fix: Replace with planted overlaps of different sizes including a subset set (the planted 8-set table in data/ is a drop-in known-answer test) and state the expected bar heights in the Skill.

recommendations.title: Package masking, stray axes, labels and export claims
recommendations.problem: ComplexUpset and UpSetR both export upset(); attaching ComplexUpset second breaks the UpSetR block with 'unused arguments' (matters for the 'migrate UpSetR to ComplexUpset' prompt). The shipped first Python plot calls plt.subplots then plot(fig=fig), leaving an empty axes drawn over the figure. ComplexUpset leaves the x label 'group'. Usage-guide step 8 (cairo_pdf / Type-42) is implemented nowhere: matplotlib's default pdf.fonttype is 3 and the R example uses pdf().
recommendations.fix: Use ComplexUpset::upset / UpSetR::upset in the migration text, replace plt.subplots by plt.figure, set xlab, and add rcParams['pdf.fonttype'] = 42 and cairo_pdf to the export snippets.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md and usage-guide.md duplicate the same tips
recommendations.problem: The usage-guide Tips section and Quick Start restate the SKILL.md failure modes almost verbatim (ggplot2 4.0 note, cap at 20-25, unique(), degree vs cardinality, upset_query), so both load for one task.
recommendations.root_cause: No split between method and quick-start content.
recommendations.fix: Keep the tips once in SKILL.md and reduce usage-guide.md to prompts, or move failure modes to a references/ file.
